name: JSON Data Drift Analyzer
tagline: Turns "something looks off about this run" into an evidenced answer.
summary: A browser-first QA tool for scraped-data pipeline exports. Upload a known-good baseline and a suspect latest export; it diffs them record by record, separates systemic field loss (a broken selector) from scattered drift, recovers only what a per-source policy allows, routes everything else to a human decision queue with an append-only log, and produces six audit-ready artifacts with a SHA-256 manifest. Everything runs in a Web Worker in your browser. No backend, no upload, no telemetry.

data.angle: Diffs two pipeline exports record by record, separates systemic field loss from scattered drift, and recovers only what a per-source policy allows, with provenance on every value.

swe.angle: 33k lines of TypeScript and React 19 with 2,682 test assertions, Playwright end-to-end runs that include axe accessibility checks, a Web Worker analysis path and a build-time Content Security Policy.

highlights: Matching is exact and deterministic: primary key first, fallback keys over the remainder, ambiguity judged against the whole reference population so a fallback can never pick the wrong record.
QA reports, never acts. Automation may only backfill a policy-approved field that is strictly blank with exactly one baseline match; overwriting a value takes a person and a reason.

Source profiles resolve in layers: one base policy, one small delta per source, local overrides that are flagged stale when the repo moves on. A policy hash is stamped into every finding, decision and export.
Analysis runs once in a Web Worker, is cached in IndexedDB keyed by file hashes and configuration, and every large table is virtualised.
Every export passes a secret scan before it is handed back; over plain HTTP the app says it cannot prove which files it read rather than hiding it.
